audit_scope: Read-only ordinary Trainer dtype/optimizer/JIT path evidence, no compilation or new hardware run

findings.evidence: loss wrapper casts compute model under shared compute context for both modes; _train_step computes grads once and take_step before optional hooks
findings.limitation: The two compilations can still fuse differently when diagnostic hook outputs extend the result.

findings.evidence: _jit_train_step_fn_no_hook sets _no_hooks=True and is the step_fn used for lowering, first ordinary update, warmups, timed steps, and profiled steps
findings.limitation: Native uses ordinary jax.jit Explicit mesh; legacy uses named_jit Auto mesh, the intended comparison.

findings.evidence: Shared cast_params_by_trainability places trainables in policy parameter dtype and nontrainables in compute dtype; benchmark policy has float32 master params and BF16 or FP32 compute
findings.limitation: Source logic alone does not prove every compiled intermediate dtype or context is equal.

findings.evidence: First ordinary no-hook new_state params and Adam mu/nu/count copied independently to host before subsequent state donation. These are compared and physical layouts enforced.
findings.limitation: Gradient arrays are captured only from hook executable. Loss group is hook-executable first loss; normal first loss exists as result.loss but is not separately retained in report.

conclusion: No new Trainer source math/dtype discrepancy identified. Retained normal moment evidence can independently test whether backward divergence persists without hooks; await agent tensor-level audit. Do not claim isolated diagnostic establishes full-Trainer backward identity.
